evidence.says: Donald W. Jones, author of both books, is an adjunct classics professor at the University of Tennessee and an economic consultant.
Don Jones served on the University of Central Arkansas history faculty from 1968 to 2018 and earned a University of Kansas doctorate in 1994.

basis: The book author and the Central Arkansas historian have distinct, overlapping academic and professional careers. The latter's 1994 doctorate matches the thesis on key b; the publisher identifies the author of both books on key a.

evidence.says: The 2005 report names Christian Schwan in its byline, but its citation and author metadata name Annette Schuhmann; it identifies Schuhmann as a ZZF researcher.
Annette Schuhmann's ZZF profile lists Kulturarbeit im sozialistischen Betrieb (2006) and Netzwerke lokaler Eliten in der DDR.

basis: The report's conflicting byline and metadata leave its authorship uncertain. Its discussion of the ZZF researcher and her related publication does not establish that she wrote the report credited to key b.

evidence.says: The catalogue attributes an H-SAfrica review of Intermediaries, Interpreters, and Clerks to Tamba Mbayo.
Tamba M'bayo is the author of Muslim Interpreters in Colonial Senegal and is affiliated with West Virginia University.

basis: The sources identify the reviewer and the book author but do not establish a connection between their works or careers. The shared name and subject alone do not meet the identity standard.

evidence.says: Smithsonian Libraries lists Land into landscape (1985) by John Michael Hunter, born 1932.
The bibliography lists Land into landscape and The Essex landscape under John Michael Hunter.

basis: The sources identify the book author but do not connect him to John Hunter's 1959 Harvard history dissertation. The evidence does not establish either a shared identity or two distinct people.

evidence.says: Dominique Brégent-Heald reviewed Holiday in Mexico for H-Travel in August 2012.
In 2006, Dominique Brégent-Heald was at Memorial University and working on Reel Borders.

basis: The H-Travel review identifies its author but does not provide an affiliation or a link to the works on the other key. The sources found do not establish that the two keys represent the same person.

evidence.says: Brian Jirout reviewed Exploration and Engineering for H-Sci-Med-Tech in November 2015.
Georgia Tech lists Brian Jirout and the dissertation One Space Age Development for the World: The American Landsat Civil Remote Sensing Program in Use, 1953-2003.

basis: The review identifies its author but does not give an affiliation linking him to the Georgia Tech dissertation. The matching name and subject alone do not establish identity.

evidence.says: Thomas Williams of Oxford's Faculty of History reviewed The Shameful Peace in June 2009.
Cites Thomas Williams, Remaking the Franco-German Borderlands, DPhil, University of Oxford, 2010.
Thomas Williams received a Rice history PhD in 2000 for Getting Organized; he later edited an astronomy encyclopedia and coauthored an astronomy history.

basis: The Oxford reviewer's institution and date match the author of the 2010 Oxford DPhil, while the other key belongs to a Rice PhD whose documented subsequent career was in the history of astronomy. The identification of the reviewer with the Oxford DPhil author is inferred from the institution and timing, so the difference is assessed at medium confidence.

evidence.says: Jennifer L. Ball wrote Byzantine Dress and received a Ph.D. in Byzantine art from NYU in 2001; she was a Princeton fellow in 2002–03.
Jennifer Lynne Ball wrote The Twilight of the Era of Hush and Pretend as a Purdue Ph.D. dissertation in American history.
Cites Jennifer Ball's The Twilight of the Era of Hush and Pretend as a 2005 Purdue history Ph.D. dissertation.

basis: The book author earned a 2001 NYU doctorate in Byzantine art and held a Princeton fellowship in 2002–03; the thesis author earned a separate Purdue history doctorate in 2005. The distinct doctorates and overlapping careers support different people.

evidence.says: Helen Brooks lists Actresses, Gender and the Eighteenth Century Stage and the Cambridge Companion to British Theatre of the First World War among her publications.
In its 2008 awards, the society identifies Dr Helen Brooks as a Nottingham lecturer working on Playing Women.

basis: The theatre scholar's documented career is much later than the 1948 Nebraska dissertation in the supplied AHA record. The sources found do not directly establish whether the dissertation author and theatre scholar are different people, so the long gap alone is insufficient to decide.

evidence.says: Lists Robert C. Donaldson's British Policy Toward Germany, 1932–33 as a Michigan dissertation in progress in 1952–53.
Catalogues Robert Donaldson's Patronage and the Church as a 1955 University of Edinburgh PhD thesis.

basis: The keys refer to distinct doctoral projects at different universities in closely overlapping years. This supports two scholars, although the sources do not explicitly compare the two authors.

evidence.says: William H. Hill describes his UC Berkeley doctorate and dissertation on Vissarion Belinskii and social criticism.
Cites William Steinert Hill Jr., The Business Community and National Defense, dissertation, Stanford University, 1980.

basis: The distinctive Belinskii dissertation is consistent with William H. Hill's account of his Berkeley doctorate; the other dissertation is attributed to William Steinert Hill Jr. at Stanford. The different middle names and doctorates support two people, although the first source describes rather than titles the dissertation.

evidence.says: Lists ‘Ambiguities of Dependence’: Past and Present in Southern Africa’s Political Practice by Khumisho Moguerane, published online in 2026.
Cites K. Moguerane’s A History of the Molemas as an Oxford DPhil thesis from 2014.
A 2015 workshop biography says Khumisho Moguerane completed a PhD at Oxford University.

basis: The Oxford doctorate and the 2026 article have not been linked to one person by a source identifying the article author’s degree or both works. The name and subject overlap alone do not establish identity.

evidence.says: David Kevin McDonald wrote Organizing Womanhood, a 1987 PhD dissertation at SUNY Stony Brook.
David Alexander McDonald's CV lists World City Syndrome, a 1988 HBA and a 1996 University of Toronto PhD in Political Science.

basis: The dissertation is attributed to David Kevin McDonald, while the author of World City Syndrome is David Alexander McDonald. Their documented degree histories differ: the latter's CV lists an undergraduate degree in 1988, after the former's 1987 doctorate.

evidence.says: Wayne State University Press identifies Mikelle Smith Omari-Tunkara as the author of Manipulating the Sacred and as a University of Arizona art professor.

basis: The publisher identifies the book's author, but the sources found do not independently connect that author to the review on the other key. The H-Net review page was inaccessible, so the shared name alone is insufficient to establish identity.

evidence.says: Esther Meier's works include Die Gregorsmesse and Joachim von Sandrart; her art history career includes a TU Dortmund post in 2012–2014.
Dr. Esther Meier is credited with the 2014 Baikal-Amur-Magistrale review and a 2013 conference at Helmut-Schmidt-Universität Hamburg.
Die Gregorsmesse by Esther Meier was accepted as a dissertation at Universität Marburg in 2003.
Esther Meier's dissertation project Industrialisierung in Tatarstan am Beispiel von Naberežnye Čelny is listed at Universität Hamburg.

basis: The reviewer's Hamburg history career and dissertation project differ from the art historian's Dortmund career and Marburg dissertation. Their distinct careers overlap in 2012–2014, supporting two people; the identification is inferred from the institutional records.

evidence.says: Robert L. Hilliard, author of Writing for Television, Radio, and New Media, earned a Ph.D. at Columbia University.
The bibliography cites R. Hilliard's The Genesis of the Economic and Social Program of the National Socialist Movement as a University of Iowa Ph.D. thesis, 1957.

basis: The Iowa dissertation and the broadcasting author's Columbia doctorate indicate different scholars. The conclusion is inferred from their different doctoral records; the sources do not explicitly compare them.

evidence.says: Routledge lists Robert D. Bush as author of The Louisiana Purchase: A Global Context.
A 1971 bibliography lists Robert D. Bush of Lawrence, Kansas, and the dissertation Individualism and the Role of the Individual in British and French Socialism.

basis: Both works are attributed to Robert D. Bush, but the sources found do not connect the dissertation author to the author of the Louisiana book. The shared name and compatible dates alone are insufficient to establish identity.

evidence.says: Copyright records list Wilhelm Dilthey as historiographer (1955) and Hermann Cohen: the challenge of a religion of reason (1984) under William Kluback.
The CiNii author record lists Wilhelm Dilthey's philosophy of history (1956) and The legacy of Hermann Cohen (1989) by William Kluback.

basis: The copyright listings give the same name for works on both sides, and the CiNii record connects a 1956 Dilthey book with a work on the first key. Neither source establishes that the 1955 dissertation and the 1956 book are the same work or that their authors are the same person.

evidence.says: Rivka B. Kern Ulmer is credited with A Synoptic Edition of Pesiqta Rabbati and an affiliation at Bucknell University.
The bibliography credits Rivka B. Ulmer with the 1999 H-Judaic review of Agendas for the Study of Midrash.

basis: The publisher identifies the author of a work on key a, and a bibliography identifies the reviewer on key b, but the sources found do not link the review to that author's works or establish the UCLA affiliation for the author. The similar names and subject are insufficient to establish identity.

evidence.says: Lists Frank Becker and Elke Reinhardt-Becker as editors of Mythos USA (2006).
Credits Ralf Blank with a review of Fachinformation und EDV-Arbeitstechniken für Historiker, dated 12 January 2001.

basis: No source found connects the book editor to the review credited to the second key. The located review of the same title is credited to someone else and is dated January, so it does not establish the identity of the February review credit.

evidence.says: Matthias Müller’s Die SPD und die Vertriebenenverbände is also a 2011 University of Gießen dissertation.
Lists Matthias Müller as author of the conference report Arbeitswelten und Arbeitsbeziehungen, Bonn, 8–9 October 2009.

basis: The sources identify the book author and the conference report author, but do not establish that they are the same person. The shared name and related subject are insufficient to merge the keys.

evidence.says: Bernd Gehrke, born 1950, edited both ...das war doch nicht unsere Alternative and Der betriebliche Aufbruch im Herbst 1989.

basis: The institutional publication identifies the editor of the works on side a, but I found no source linking that person to the review credit on side b. The shared name and subject do not establish identity.

evidence.says: Werner Maleczek's bibliography lists Petrus Capuanus, Kardinal, Legat am Vierten Kreuzzug, Theologe, Vienna 1988.
The 2013 MIÖG contents list a review of Rom und die Regionen under Herwig Weigl.

basis: The university bibliography establishes the author of the book on side a, but I could not verify the attribution of the H-Net review on side b or find a source linking it to that author. A separate 2013 review of the same volume has a different reviewer, so the reviewed title alone cannot resolve the credit.

evidence.says: Kenneth Dzutsumwa Manungo wrote The Role Peasants Played in the Zimbabwe War of Liberation, a 1991 Ohio University PhD dissertation.

basis: The dissertation record supplies the reviewer's full name, but I found no source linking the dissertation to the specific review or its author's institutional career. The name match alone does not establish identity under the brief's criteria.

evidence.says: Lists William Evan Price's Wilkes-Barre dissertation at Kent State University in 1979.
Names William S. Price, Jr. as editor of North Carolina Higher-Court Records, 1702–1708, published in 1974.

basis: The Wilkes-Barre dissertation is by William Evan Price, while the matching North Carolina court-records volume is credited to William S. Price, Jr. The incompatible middle names indicate different scholars; the link from the 1973 thesis record to the 1974 volume is inferred from their distinctive matching titles.

evidence.says: Heinz P. Wassermann reviewed Transnationale Gedächtnisorte in Zentraleuropa for H-Museum in 2003.
Heinz P. Wassermann's Zuviel Vergangenheit tut nicht gut! is a revised part of his 1998 Graz dissertation.

basis: The review credit supplies the same middle initial as the book author, and the record associates the reviewer with Graz. The sources found do not establish that the reviewer and book author are the same person or place the reviewer at the dissertation institution in the relevant years.

evidence.says: Jessica Martin, author of Walton's Lives, is identified as a fellow and college lecturer at Trinity College, Cambridge.
Jessica Martin wrote Walton's Lives, earned a Cambridge PhD in 1993, and was a Trinity College lecturer and fellow from 1999 to 2010.

basis: The AHA record identifies the other Jessica Martin's 2006 history dissertation at the University of Colorado Boulder. The distinct doctorates and overlapping Cambridge and Colorado careers strongly indicate different scholars.

evidence.says: Ann Elizabeth Pfau wrote Miss Yourlovin: Women in the Culture of American World War II Soldiers at Rutgers University in 2001.

basis: The AHA identifies the dissertation author, but the sources found do not establish that she also wrote the H-War review. The shared name and subject alone do not establish identity.

evidence.says: Jim MacPherson lists Women and the Irish Nation (2012) and Migration and the Female Orange Order (2012) among his publications.

basis: The university page identifies the author of works on side b, but the available evidence does not connect him to the 2008 H-Albion review on side a. The H-Net review page could not be accessed to check its author details.

evidence.says: Subho Basu reviewed Bangladesh and Pakistan: Flirting with Failure in South Asia for H-Asia in September 2012.
McGill associate professor Subho Basu is the author of Does Class Matter? (2004).

basis: The review identifies its author by name but gives no affiliation or other link to the author of Does Class Matter? The available evidence does not establish that the two keys represent the same person.

evidence.says: Jeffrey O’Leary reviewed From Liberation to Conquest for H-SHGAPE in April 2012.
Jeffrey O'Leary's Manufacturing Reality is listed as a 2015 Kent State University history dissertation.

basis: The sources identify the review and dissertation but do not establish that their authors are the same person. The shared name and compatible subject are insufficient to merge the keys.
